column1: # ci_emulator.tsv — THE EMULATOR-TIER REGISTRY (14z-128). One row per gate under
# tests/ that needs MAME, FBNeo or the Verilator simulator, i.e. every script
# that tests/run_all_static.sh's classifier calls emulator-tier. It is the
# input to tests/run_all_emulator.sh and the ONLY place a release's emulator
# WHY IT EXISTS. Measured at the 14z-127 close: 164 emulator-tier gates, 32 of
# them reachable from any runner. The other 132 could be run only by typing a
# filename, so nothing would even ASK them at release. The maintainer's release
# policy (STATE "RELEASE-TIME TEST SCOPE", 2026-09-02) is that at release ALL
# tests run and "anything red, anything skipped is a hard fail" — a policy that
# cannot operate over a set nobody enumerates.
# COLUMNS   gate <TAB> lane <TAB> scope <TAB> cadence <TAB> args <TAB> note
#           prereq = the instrument and verdict-logic ground truths ([VSP-19]);
#           they run FIRST because a moved instrument invalidates every result
#           after it ([CPE-24]). The other three are the three implementations.
#           release = its SUBJECT is the released artifact (legacy content
#           inside it included — an oracle leg on vsav2 or pristine vsavj is a
#           out     = out of RELEASE scope by the maintainer's discriminator.
#           OUT IS NOT "DELETE" AND NOT "DO NOT RUN": run_all_emulator.sh
#           --scope all runs these too, and the sweep is how they are kept
#           honest. It only means they do not gate a release.
#   cadence romset | bitstream — WHAT MOVING THING THE GATE FOLLOWS, which is
#           a DIFFERENT question from whether it gates a release.
#           romset    = its subject moves when the romset moves, so it runs at
#                       every freeze AND at every release. The default; 158 of
#           bitstream = its subject is the CORE/BITSTREAM, which moves on its
#                       own cadence (the .rbf has not moved since 14z-108 while
#                       the romset moved many times). Runs at every RELEASE,
#                       and at a freeze ONLY when the freeze targets MiSTer.
#           RULED 2026-09-03 by the maintainer, as the same rule already made
#           for the stock control MRA ("run once per new .rbf (seed / slice /
#           pin), NOT per romset release" — STATE "DOES THE STOCK CONTROL MRA
#           STILL HAVE A USE?"). Verbatim: "it should be applied ALWAYS on
#           release but not for a freeze, UNLESS explicitly in scope, typically
#           because the changes target MiSTer specifically. If such an
#           automation is unrealistic, the question should be asked at freeze
#           if it should be included."  IT IS AUTOMATED: `--freeze`
#           (= --cadence romset) drops them and NAMES what it dropped, so the
#           question is asked by the runner rather than remembered.
#           Only a `mister` lane row may be `bitstream` (enforced).
#           THE TWO MiSTer EXCEPTIONS ARE DELIBERATE: test_mister_sdram_census
#           and test_mister_gfxc_fetch measure where THIS ROMSET lands in
#           SDRAM, so they follow the romset and run at every freeze.
#   args    the invocation. `-` = the gate's OWN defaults, deliberately: what a
#           release run would actually hit is what the sweep must measure
#           ([VSP-95] — a path-named default is a dated assertion with no
#           expiry). Tokens shaped VAR=value before the script are passed as
#           %HUI% %PYR% %STOCK% expand to the build set under test.
#   note    for scope=out the REASON, and it must lead with one keyword:
#             romset:      the subject is a reference romset's own behaviour
#                          (vanilla vsavj or native vs2), not ours
#             platform:    the subject is another platform
#             momentary:   a specific probe for one investigation
#             dev-ladder:  the subject is a scratch dev build, not the artifact
#           for scope=release, free text (a runtime hint, a known trap).
# THE CLASSIFICATION IS RULED (maintainer, 2026-09-03) — 141 release, 23 out.
# Every `out` row states its reason so the judgement stays checkable row by row
# rather than argued in bulk. The three judgement calls the proposal flagged
# were each ruled, and each is recorded where it applies:
#   (a) THE TWO #113 GATES -> release, against the letter of the subject
#       discriminator. "51s is basically nothing for a release and still not
#       enough cost not to run every time we freeze honestly." Their rows carry
#   (b) THE MiSTer LANE -> release scope KEPT, but split onto the `bitstream`
#       cadence above, so a release always pays it and a freeze only does when
#   (c) THE FOUR dev-ladder GATES -> stay `out`. test_m3a_reproducible is the
#       real pipeline lock on the released artifact and is already release.
# TWO THINGS `out` DOES NOT MEAN, both affirmed by the maintainer the same day:
#   * `out` IS NOT "resolved". audit_hitclass_map_cost is `out` AND is one of
#     the two DEAD MUST-FIRE CONTROLS — the class that goes green while
#     asserting nothing ([VSP-19]). Scope and control-health are orthogonal.
#     audit_phase_mode_cost are red RIGHT NOW with exact diagnoses; their `out`
#     classing is only what keeps them from blocking.
# COMPLETENESS IS ENFORCED BOTH WAYS by run_all_emulator.sh: an emulator-tier
# script with no row is UNREGISTERED, a row whose script is gone is DEAD.
